title: Initial-object criterion for a map between left fibrations
statement: Use quasicategories, simplicial functors, coherent natural equivalences, initial objects and internal functor simplicial sets from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and left fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ and $q:F\to B$ be left fibrations of quasicategories in one sufficiently large fixed universe. Let $u:E\to F$ be a simplicial map with $qu=p$, and let $e\in E$ be initial. If $u(e)$ is initial in $F$, then $u$ is an equivalence of quasicategories over $B$: there is a simplicial map $v:F\to E$ with $pv=q$ and coherent natural equivalences $vu\simeq\operatorname{id}_E$ and $uv\simeq\operatorname{id}_F$ over $B$. Here a coherent natural equivalence over $B$ is an equivalence in the simplicial set of functors over $B$: in degree $n$ its maps $E\times\Delta^n\to E$ or $F\times\Delta^n\to F$ compose to $p\operatorname{pr}_E$ or $q\operatorname{pr}_F$, respectively, including the inverse-equivalence witnesses.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.6.20, sufficient direction and proof: the inverse functor and inverse equivalences are constructed in functor categories over the common base. Kerodon tag 03J6, not the unrelated Stacks tag. Online statement and proof read; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: Put $b=p(e)=q(u(e))$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-initial-evaluation-trivial-fibration] with source $F$, initial object $u(e)$ and target left fibration $E\to B$. Evaluation $\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(F,E)\to E_b$ is a trivial Kan fibration. Its vertex surjectivity [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] gives a simplicial map $v:F\to E$ over $B$ satisfying $v(u(e))=e$ exactly. In particular $pv=q$.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.6.20, sufficient direction, made explicit using Proposition 5.6.6.19 (038R), implication (2) => (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-initial-evaluation-trivial-fibration] with source and target $E\to B$ and initial object $e$. The vertices $vu$ and $\operatorname{id}_E$ of $M=\operatorname{Fun}_{/B}(E,E)$ both evaluate to $e$. Lift the boundary $\partial\Delta^1\to M$ with those ordered endpoints over the degenerate edge at $e$ to obtain $\alpha:vu\to\operatorname{id}_E$. Lift the reversed endpoints over the same degenerate edge to obtain $\alpha^{\prime}:\operatorname{id}_E\to vu$. These lifts exist by [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. For the ordered vertex triple $(vu,\operatorname{id}_E,vu)$ prescribe the consecutive edges $\alpha,\alpha^{\prime}$ and the long edge $\operatorname{id}_{vu}$. Their evaluations are all constant at $e$, so the entire boundary lies above the constant $2$-simplex at $e$ and lifts to a $2$-simplex in $M$. For the ordered triple $(\operatorname{id}_E,vu,\operatorname{id}_E)$ prescribe consecutive edges $\alpha^{\prime},\alpha$ and the degenerate long edge at $\operatorname{id}_E$. These three edges agree at their vertices and evaluate to the boundary of the constant $2$-simplex at $e$, so a second boundary lift gives the other inverse triangle. By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], $\alpha$ is a coherent natural equivalence $vu\simeq\operatorname{id}_E$; every edge and triangle is over $B$.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.6.20, sufficient direction, made explicit using Proposition 5.6.6.19 (038R), implication (2) => (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-initial-evaluation-trivial-fibration] with source and target $F\to B$ and initial object $u(e)$. The two vertices $uv$ and $\operatorname{id}_F$ evaluate to the same vertex, since $uv(u(e))=u(e)$. Lift the two ordered boundaries with endpoints $(uv,\operatorname{id}_F)$ and $(\operatorname{id}_F,uv)$ over the constant edge at $u(e)$, obtaining $\beta$ and $\beta^{\prime}$. For the ordered triple $(uv,\operatorname{id}_F,uv)$ prescribe consecutive edges $\beta,\beta^{\prime}$ and the degenerate long edge at $uv$. For the ordered triple $(\operatorname{id}_F,uv,\operatorname{id}_F)$ prescribe consecutive edges $\beta^{\prime},\beta$ and the degenerate long edge at $\operatorname{id}_F$. Each prescribed boundary is well-defined because the edges agree at their endpoints. Both boundaries evaluate to the constant $2$-simplex at $u(e)$; the boundary-lifting property [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration] supplies their fillers. Hence [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives a coherent natural equivalence $uv\simeq\operatorname{id}_F$ with both inverse witnesses over $B$.

source.place: Corollary 5.6.6.20, sufficient direction, made explicit using Proposition 5.6.6.19 (038R), implication (2) => (3).

proof.text: The constructed $v$ satisfies $pv=q$, and the two constructed equivalence edges and all their inverse witnesses belong to the respective simplicial sets of functors over $B$. These are precisely the quasi-inverse data in the definition of functor equivalence [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus $u$ is an equivalence over $B$, with exactly the strict base compatibility and coherent inverse data asserted.

lean.statement: theorem initial_left_fibration_equivalence {E F B : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory E] [Quasicategory F] [Quasicategory B] (p : E ⟶ B) (q : F ⟶ B) (u : E ⟶ F) (hp : leftFibration p) (hq : leftFibration q) (hu : u ≫ q = p) (e : E.obj (op ⦋0⦌)) (he : IsInitial E e) (hue : IsInitial F (u.app (op ⦋0⦌) e)) : ∃ v : F ⟶ E, v ≫ p = q ∧ IsNaturallyEquivalentOver p (u ≫ v) (𝟙 E) ∧ IsNaturallyEquivalentOver q (v ≫ u) (𝟙 F)
